title: Graffiti Artist
text:
Title: Graffiti Artist
 I’m on a train in the French countryside. Sitting directly across from me is my brother 
 Jim. We pass a centuries-old cottage in the middle of a field. 
 The side of the cottage facing us features two words, each pitifully rendered in 
 spray-paint on weathered stone. Before he settled down and started a family, Jim was once an 
 extremely prolific graffiti artist whose work can still be viewed all over the post-industrial 
 ruins of St. Louis City. He says that in the United States, you don’t normally see 
 graffiti out in the country. It’s sort of an unwritten rule: writers don’t paint 
 outside of metropolitan areas. I nod in agreement, adding that using historical
  structures as your canvas is… 
 offensive isn’t the word… inappropriate? Jim agrees, and the conversation ends there.
